label: Conflict events with deaths (UCDP)
notes: Organised violence events with at least one death, sized by the number killed.
details: Organized-violence events with >=1 death. type: state_based / non_state / one_sided; deaths = best estimate; where_prec 1=exact .. 3=county, >=4 coarse (admin-1/country). oil_related = keyword match on oil fields/pipelines (1 inside SSD; 5 cross-border oil events e.g. Heglig added with inside_ssd=false). Temporal: event layer - single `date`; valid_from = valid_to = its month (date verified 2018-01..2025-12).

label: Attacks on aid, health and education (Insecurity Insight)
source: Insecurity Insight (Security in Numbers Database) via HDX, CC BY-SA 4.0
notes: Reported incidents affecting aid workers, health care, education and sexual violence. Locations are only approximate, often the centre of a state.
details: One point per incident 2018-2025 with `date`, `type`, `victims`. LOW GEOLOCATION PRECISION: the source censors coordinates, so points sit at the centroid of the reported state / administrative area (`geo_precision`), stacked on top of each other - do not read them as incident locations. Records with no state ('No Information') or outside South Sudan are dropped from the layer. Temporal: event layer - single `date`; valid_from = valid_to = its month (date verified 2018-01..2025-12).

label: Logistics hubs and common storage
source: WFP Logistics Cluster, South Sudan Concept of Operations maps Jan 2018 - Jun 2026 (16 dated maps)
notes: Humanitarian logistics hubs and shared warehouses, shown for the periods they appear on the Logistics Cluster's operations maps.
details: Temporal: one feature per site and period with constant storage capacity/manager; valid_from/valid_to from consecutive map dates (2018-01, 2019-01/06/09, 2020-03/04/08, 2021-05/10, 2022-09, 2023-01/04/09, 2026-02/03/06). No map Oct 2023-Jan 2026: sites carried through (date_basis says so). type = Logistics Cluster hub (coordination/transport services) / cluster common storage / partner-managed MSU; storage_m2 as printed. Coordinates = town (OCHA gazetteer) or map pin (coord_quality='approximate'), not the warehouse itself.

label: UN peacekeeping bases (UNMISS)
source: Geo-PKO v2.3 (UN maps 4456 Rev.30 Nov 2017 .. Rev.61 Oct 2024) + UN Geospatial map 4456 Rev.62 (Jan 2025) and Rev.67 (Jan 2026)
notes: UN peacekeeping deployments in each period, with approximate troop numbers from UN deployment maps.
details: One feature per location and period with constant role / troop estimate (rounded to 10) / FPU presence; valid_from/valid_to from consecutive 4456 map revisions (38 maps). troops_est = Geo-PKO estimate from unit sizes (approximate); fpu_present = formed police unit at location. 2025 periods from Rev.62 have no troop numbers. Closures: Aweil Nov 2025 (documented), Yei & Torit between Jul 2025 (Rev.65) and Jan 2026 (Rev.67) -> valid_to 2025-12; Tambura closed Jan 2026 (open through 2025). PoC sites: see crisis-sites layer.

label: Monitored food markets (WFP)
notes: Markets where WFP recorded food prices, shown for the months they were monitored.
details: Temporal: valid_from/valid_to = first/last month with retail prices 2018-01..2025-12; gaps longer than 6 months split a market into separate periods. valid_from null = already monitored before 2018. months_with_prices counts reporting months within the period.

label: Protection of civilians sites and camps
source: Curated: OSM (HOT/HDX) coordinates; UNMISS / UNHCR / IOM public site lists; UNMISS press releases on PoC redesignation (2020-21)
notes: UN protection of civilians sites, displacement camps and refugee camps, including when sites were handed over or closed.
details: Temporal: one feature per site and status period. PoC -> IDP camp redesignation: Bor & Wau Sep 2020 (documented), Juba PoC1/3 Nov 2020 and Bentiu Mar 2021 (month approximate); Wau former PoC closed 2021 (month unknown); Malakal stays a PoC site; Renk transit centre from Apr 2023. Other camps opened before 2018 and are open-ended. Logistics hubs moved to the logcluster_hubs layer. `coord_quality` flags approximate positions. Not exhaustive (see DTM layer).
status_values: redesignated IDP camp under government control
redesignated IDP camp; expanded after 2021-22 floods
opened with arrivals from Sudan after 15 Apr 2023

label: Health facilities (registry status over time)
source: MoH health facility lists 2016 and 2023, IOM DTM village assessment 2019-20, WHO Master Facility List Mar 2024 (HDX); team compilation (Nov 2026)
notes: Hospitals and clinics with their registry status in each period. The status comes from comparing the 2016, 2019-20, 2023 and 2024 facility lists and adding documented closures. Being on a list does not prove a facility was working.
details: Status periods from MoH Apr 2016 list, IOM DTM village assessment Aug 2019-Mar 2020 (7 counties), MoH 2023 master list and WHO MFL Mar 2024, matched by name and distance; 'new since 2016' facilities start at the first list that has them (opened between Apr 2016 and that list); facilities dropped by 2023 are 'unconfirmed' to Dec 2023; Ulang (closed 14 Apr 2025) and Old Fangak (bombed 3 May 2025) documented. 461 matched facilities lack coordinates and are not mapped. About 11.5% of 'new since 2016' sit within 300 m of a 2016 facility (likely renamed). Aggregate 2022 and 2025 aid-cut closures are timeline events. Superseded the WHO-MFL snapshot layer (all its points are included).
status_values: non-functional in 2016 (dropped from the registry by 2023)

label: Water points (last known status)
source: Water Point Data Exchange WPDx-Basic (OCHA/WASH WIMS 2006-13, ACF/RWSS 2016, Water for South Sudan 2011-15, UNHCR 2019), CC BY 4.0
notes: Boreholes and other water points with their last reported working status. Most of these reports date from before 2018 and may be out of date.
details: Temporal: valid_from = install year if >= 2018 (none in the data: install years <= 2015 or unknown) else null; valid_to null (decommissioning not recorded). status = functional status at status_report_date; almost all reports predate 2018 (status_stale=true: last known status, not current). UNHCR camp points reported Sep 2019 get a separate status period from 2019-09. Not a complete inventory of current water points.
status_values: not reported before first in-window report

label: Schools (status over time)
source: SSSAMS 2015 list and 2019 enrolment export (HDX, CC0), IOM DTM village assessment 2019-20, OpenStreetMap (ODbL); team compilation (Nov 2026)
notes: Schools with their status from the 2015 and 2019 school lists, the 2019-20 village assessment and the 2020-21 COVID-19 closure. There is no school-level data after May 2021, so later statuses are carried forward.
details: SSSAMS 2015 list (coordinates) + SSSAMS 29 Oct 2019 enrolment export (joined on school code) + IOM DTM Aug 2019-Mar 2020 (392 DTM-only points, a few may duplicate SSSAMS); national COVID-19 closure 2020-03..2021-04; base status carried forward from 2021-05 (flagged 'presumed'). 2015 managed/enrolment-by-sex kept from the old layer. OpenStreetMap schools > 300 m from any SSSAMS/DTM school kept as undated. Heatwave closures (Mar 2024, Feb-Mar 2025) and flood closures are timeline events, not per-school periods.

label: Migration monitoring points (IOM)
source: IOM DTM South Sudan Flow Monitoring Registry (team unified dataset)
notes: Places where IOM counted people on the move, shown for the months they reported.
details: Where FMR counts travellers; FMR numbers depend on these locations. Temporal: valid_from/valid_to = first/last month with recorded internal forced trips (Jan 2020-Aug 2025); >6 empty months split a point into periods; Nov 2023-Dec 2024 (no public data) is bridged. Points still active in Aug 2025 are open-ended. active_months / travellers summarise each period.

source: UNFPA South Sudan annual reports 2022-2024, newsletters and situation reports; UNICEF; UN Peacebuilding Fund evaluation; UNMISS; South Sudan Medical Journal; host facility coordinates from the WHO Master Facility List
details: Month-by-month status from dated evidence: 'named in a source' between two dated mentions of the centre (UNFPA 2018/2020 lists, UNICEF May 2020, UN Peacebuilding Fund evaluation Nov 2021, UNMISS Oct 2023, South Sudan Medical Journal Nov 2023, UNFPA newsletters Q1 2024 and Q1 2025, UNFPA situation report Feb-Mar 2025); 'UNFPA reports 13 centres' where only UNFPA's yearly nationwide count (annual reports 2021-2024; the 2024 paragraph repeats 2023) covers it - this applies only to the 12 UNFPA-network centres; 'status unconfirmed' after the last evidence (hollow marker). Akobo one-stop centre (UN Peacebuilding Fund, 2021) and the Juba and Wau safe houses (UNFPA 2022-2024) were added; Yei is UNICEF-supported. Some first dates (Dec 2019 and Dec 2021 ELRP tables, UNFPA 2021 annual report) come from the team compilation and were not re-checked. No dated, machine-readable GBV service map exists for women and girls' friendly spaces or protection desks.
label: Gender-based violence (GBV) one-stop centres
notes: Hospital centres where survivors of sexual and gender-based violence can get medical care, counselling, and legal and police help in one place, plus three safe houses. Each is shown from the first report that it was working. UNFPA reported 13 centres every year up to 2024 but named only a few after 2020 (Juba in 2023, Wau up to early 2025, Malakal and Bentiu in early 2025). For these centres a hollow marker means no source has confirmed the centre since it was last mentioned. It does not mean the centre closed.
status_values: operating (this centre named in a source)
operating (not named in this period; covered by UNFPA's nationwide count of 13 or by a later mention)
status unconfirmed (no source since its last mention)

source: Sign of Hope (Feb 2020) spill investigation; PAX (2023); New Lines/Placemark (2026); Kenyatta University sampling as reported; team compilation (Nov 2026)
details: Spills on the Unity-Heglig export pipeline ~24 Aug 2019 (~2 million L) and ~28 Oct 2019 (~4 million L), GPS from Sign of Hope; after repair shown as spill site (removal not documented). Reports: flooded Block 2 wells (PAX 2023: 159 wells ~41% submerged; New Lines/Placemark 2026: 50+ of ~400 Unity wells underwater) placed at the Unity field; Kenyatta University river samples near Bentiu/Rotriak (lead up to 18 ug/L, hydrocarbons >5x limits; sampling dates unpublished) placed at Rotriak. Feb 2024 Petrodar spill is in Sudan -> timeline only.
label: Oil spills and pollution reports
notes: Two documented oil pipeline spills north of Bentiu in 2019, and two located reports of contaminated water and flooded wells in the Unity oil fields.

source: Sentinel-1 RTC radar (Microsoft Planetary Computer) at OpenStreetMap well locations; team analysis (Nov 2026)
details: Share of Sentinel-1 VV pixels below -15 dB in a 100-500 m ring around each of 102 OSM wells, monthly median; flagged when >= 25%. Undercounts flooded vegetation; near-zero 2021 likely an artefact (also Sentinel-1B loss Dec 2021). OSM maps ~100 of ~400 Unity wells.
label: Flood water around oil wells (radar)
notes: Mapped oil wells where satellite radar saw open flood water around the well in each period. This shows flooding, not contamination, and it misses water under vegetation.

source: NASA HLS v2 (2020-2025) and Sentinel-2 L2A (2018-2019) via Microsoft Planetary Computer; team analysis (Nov 2026)
details: Eight ~11x11 km sites; water pixels only, up to 3 clearest scenes per month. Status = NDTI (red-green)/(red+green) anomaly vs the site's median for that calendar month: > +0.04 more turbid, < -0.04 clearer (|anomaly| > 0.04 is about the top 20% of site-months). NDCI chlorophyll proxy included. 2018-19 Sentinel-2 L2A may be offset from 2020-25 HLS. Thar Jath wetland has only 15 months.
label: River and wetland water colour (satellite)
notes: Monthly satellite readings of how muddy the water is at eight river and wetland sites, compared with the usual level for that month. This tracks sediment and algae; it cannot detect oil or chemical pollution.

details: GeoEPR-2023 settlement polygons clipped to South Sudan; EPR-2023 power status (one period, 2011-2023, for all ten groups: Dinka senior partner, Nuer junior partner, Murle discriminated, the other seven powerless; no group has regional autonomy). Features 2018-01..2023-12 are coded; 2024-01..2025-12 carry the 2023 status forward and say so. Group shares of national population are EPR estimates. Armed-group links from ACD2EPR-2021.
label: Ethnic group areas and political power (EPR)
notes: Where ten major ethnic groups live and how much national political power each held in each year, as coded by the Ethnic Power Relations dataset up to 2023. The 2023 status is carried forward to later years.
status_values: senior partner in government (carried forward, not coded after 2023)
junior partner in government (carried forward, not coded after 2023)
discriminated against (carried forward, not coded after 2023)

label: Oil fields and wells (production status)
source: Global Energy Monitor GOGET (CC-BY 4.0), OpenStreetMap wells (ODbL); block status dates from Reuters, VOA, Radio Tamazuj, Sudan Tribune, Argus, AFP
notes: Oil fields and mapped wells, coloured by the documented production status of their oil block. This includes the 2018-19 restarts, the 2024 export halt and the December 2025 Heglig disruption.
details: GEM GOGET field points (attributes kept; GEM status in gem_status) with production periods reconciled to the team block timeline; 102 OSM wells (HOT Raw Data API, Nov 2026) replace the 93 undated OSM wells and get their block's status periods: Blocks 3&7 operating -> halted 2024-02..2024-12 -> resumed 2025-01; Blocks 1,2&4 shut -> partial 2018-08 (Toma South) -> operating 2019-01 -> disrupted 2025-12 (Heglig seized 8 Dec 2025); Block 5A shut -> operating 2021-06 -> disrupted 2025-12. Block assignment by location (east of 31E = 3&7; Guit/Koch/Leer/Mayendit/Panyijiar = 5A). Block-level status, not well-by-well. Gas-flare satellite check (MODIS) was inconclusive and is not used.

label: Oil pipelines (flow status)
notes: Mapped oil pipelines, coloured by the documented status of the oil block each one serves. Proposed routes are shown too, but they were never built.
details: Overture/OSM pipeline lines and GEM GOIT routes; status periods follow the oil block of each line (location rule as for wells; Greater Nile follows Blocks 1,2&4). The team's 169 OSM field-line segments all lie on these lines.

label: Natural disasters (floods, droughts, heatwaves)
notes: Floods, drought alerts and heatwaves reported in 2018-2025, one dot per affected county (or one for the whole country) for as long as the event lasted. Flood figures are people affected, as counted by the UN. Each dot sits at the county centre, not at the flooded place.
details: Floods: OCHA county tables on HDX for 2021 (13 Dec), 2022 (30 Nov), 2024 (20 Dec) and 2025 (30 Nov); 2019 and 2020 counties are those named on OCHA's flood maps (5 Nov 2019: 32 counties, 908,000 affected; 21 Oct 2020: 39 counties, state totals from the 31 Jan 2021 situation report) with IOM DTM/IRNA displacement figures for 2019. Each flood season runs from OCHA's reported start month to its last report (2021: month per county where given). No OCHA flood table or GLIDE flood event exists for 2023. Droughts: GDACS agricultural-drought alerts (European Drought Observatory), counties with >= 25% of their area in the alert polygon. Heatwaves: national school closures in March 2024 and February 2025, placed at Juba. No storm events were found in GDACS, IFRC GO or ReliefWeb for South Sudan 2018-2025. Epidemics are excluded.
source: OCHA South Sudan flood data (HDX) and flood snapshots; IOM DTM; IFRC GO; GDACS; Radio Tamazuj / AP
